kept_items.author: OpenAI
kept_items.text:
As we prepare to release Astra, we’re focused on making increasingly capable AI safe and broadly accessible.

Astra represents a significant advance in cybersecurity capability, reaching the Critical threshold under our Preparedness Framework.

We're previewing how we evaluated
kept_items.selection_reason: OpenAI says Astra reaches the Critical cybersecurity threshold under its Preparedness Framework ahead of release. Self-contained announcement post, thread checked.

kept_items.author: sama
kept_items.text:
Over the summer, we have been sprinting on safety priorities; it's more important than ever for capabilities and safeguards to advance together. We have more to do but have made a lot of progress. We are also going to be launching our next model soon.

There is an obvious tension
kept_items.selection_reason: Altman's full statement on pacing model releases against safety work; thread retrieved and confirmed self-contained.

kept_items.author: steph_palazzolo
kept_items.text:
OpenAI’s Astra AI uses a new reasoning approach called “recurrent depth.” Though it can help model costs and performance, researchers are concerned bc it obscures a model’s thinking process, making it more difficult to monitor.

w/ @amir @rocketalignment
kept_items.selection_reason: The Information reports Astra uses recurrent depth reasoning, raising monitorability concerns.

kept_items.author: merettm
kept_items.text:
I want to prevent a race into unmonitorability kicked off by confused reporting. The depth of the computation graph for our present frontier models, including Astra, is within a factor of two of GPT-4.

OpenAI has worked to preserve and utilize chain-of-thought monitoring since
kept_items.selection_reason: OpenAI researcher pushes back on the unmonitorability framing with a concrete claim about computation graph depth.

kept_items.author: bcherny
kept_items.text:
Fable 5.1 is our best model yet for coding, data analysis, computer use, design, presentations, Tag, and the hardest long-running agentic work.

This model is a pleasure to work with, and I've been using it for everything.
kept_items.selection_reason: Anthropic ships Fable 5.1 as its strongest coding and agentic model.

kept_items.author: Celeris_ai
kept_items.text:
Introducing Celeris-1 Magnus. A model built for agentic work.

On τ³-bench banking, Magnus delivers 41.2% at a 55-second median, against GPT-5.6-sol's 38.1% at 79 seconds.

It’s a hybrid diffusion model derived from qwen3.8-27b, optimized for agentic workloads.

For more info,
kept_items.selection_reason: Celeris-1 Magnus, a hybrid diffusion agentic model derived from qwen3.8-27b, with tau3-bench numbers.

kept_items.author: erinkwoo
kept_items.text:
Scoop: Gemini 3.8 Flash, code-named "Skimaki," is expected to release as soon as tomorrow. Google employees prefer it to Opus on coding in side-by-side testing. 

Other details in here, including Google ramping up its work on RL and outlook for Gemini 4:
kept_items.selection_reason: Gemini 3.8 Flash codenamed Skimaki reported imminent, preferred over Opus internally on coding.

kept_items.author: finkd
kept_items.text: Muse Voice Transcribe is MSL's first real-time audio perception model -- rolling out today. SOTA in streaming speech-to-text, it handles speaker diarization, and endpointing natively in a single model.
kept_items.selection_reason: Meta ships Muse Voice Transcribe, a real-time streaming speech-to-text model.

kept_items.author: tobi
kept_items.text:
Training tiny models for special purpose use cases works so incredibly well if you  have a great self improving recursive flywheel. Shopify ML team is on fire.

finetuned 0.8b model beats GPT 5.6-sol xhigh in this very specialized task.
kept_items.selection_reason: Shopify CEO reports a finetuned 0.8b model beating a frontier model on a specialised task.

kept_items.author: AnthropicAI
kept_items.text: This model, which we call Hacker-Opus, appears to be a reward-on-the-episode seeker: it is willing to take a variety of misaligned actions in pursuit of reward, but remains aligned in evaluations where there isn’t a clear grader.
kept_items.selection_reason: Anthropic's Hacker-Opus reward-hacking study; part of a self-contained research thread from the account.

kept_items.author: RTomMcCoy
kept_items.text:
NEW PAPER
(The result of an 8-year project!)

LLMs seem very different from symbolic systems. Yet LLMs excel in symbolic domains (e.g., language/code/math). How do they do it?

Our finding: LLM representations have implicit symbolic structure!

Link in thread 
1/n
kept_items.selection_reason: Eight-year paper finding implicit symbolic structure in LLM representations.

kept_items.author: anirudhg9119
kept_items.text:
AI research agents have a new bottleneck: they can invent experiments much faster than they can afford to run them.

Our new work asks: can an agent decide which ideas are worth the GPU time before executing them?

Introducing AI Research Preference Models (RPMs)
kept_items.selection_reason: AI Research Preference Models to triage which experiments deserve GPU time.

kept_items.author: FredaDuan
kept_items.text:
China Open-Source LLM Tracker

US$10-15B of total ARR, of which core LLM revenue (excluding Byte / Seedance) is ~$6-8B.

Growth has been phenomenal. Take Zhipu as an example (more data available as a public co.) ARR has grown 6x+ since March, while token usage is up >40x YTD.
kept_items.selection_reason: China open-source LLM revenue tracker with Zhipu ARR growth figures.

kept_items.author: AndrewCurran_
kept_items.text: Sam Altman to Alex Heath: 'I did not think we would be on a short-term trajectory to superintelligence a year ago. Now I think it may happen.'
kept_items.selection_reason: Altman tells Alex Heath superintelligence may now be on a short-term trajectory.

kept_items.author: distortgeekin
kept_items.text:
Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind:

"I see a lot of people setting off dozens of agents for 40 hours

I'm not sure the output justifies that level of input going in"

"We're kind of using duct tape right now. Shove it all in the context window"

In 41 minutes at Y Combinator
kept_items.selection_reason: Hassabis questions the value of long multi-agent runs and calls current context handling duct tape.

kept_items.author: kimmonismus
kept_items.text:
Thats going to be interesting. They took the safety layer out of GLM-5.3 and turned it into an admin panel.

Abliterationai’s model handles cyber work that mainstream APIs often refuse. Customers can then add their own rules through a separate policy gateway.

It is questionable
kept_items.selection_reason: Abliterated GLM-5.3 variant repackages the removed safety layer as an admin policy gateway.
